subject: A67CE51FE17BE08F286E8F8342D4C327
introduction: Bahá’u’lláh wrote that among the special bounties of this dispensation is that the faith of a child brings forgiveness to parents who did not believe; and many who wrote to ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asked first of all for a prayer for a father or mother, often one who had died. This guide gathers the answers. The fifth commandment is their root; the Qur’an supplies the very words, “My Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little”, and Noah’s prayer for his parents. Ezekiel’s teaching that each soul answers for itself, and Jesus’s “who is my mother?”, are the two points at which scripture qualifies the tie.
questions: What do children owe parents that can only be paid in prayer?
The readings say a child’s faith benefits a parent after death. What picture of the next life does that imply?
How do you pray for a parent with whom things were difficult?

outside.why: Grant his father and mother a place in Your shelter. Honour thy father and thy mother.

She reared me, and I did not recompense her. The Qur’an gives the prayer: lower unto them the wing of submission through mercy, and say: my Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little.
Proverbs on what a mother’s rearing leaves with her child: forsake not the law of thy mother.
For your noble father and mother I besought infinite favours. Honour thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise.
We beseech God to draw thy father nigh. When he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran.
Have mercy on the mother of this servant. Her children arise up, and call her blessed.
I implore Thy forgiveness. Noah’s prayer in the Qur’an: my Lord! Forgive me and my parents and him who entereth my house believing.
Immerse the parents of this servant in the oceans of Thy forgiveness. It was an holy and good thought to pray for the dead.

A son’s faith brings favour on his parents. Ezekiel insisted that guilt does not pass between generations: the soul that sinneth, it shall die. The readings hold that grace does pass, from child to parent. Why should mercy cross where blame may not?

Entreating for parents. Jesus, told that his mother and brethren stood without: whosoever shall do the will of my Father, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother. How do these prayers hold family love and the wider family of faith together?

shortfall: Readings 4, 7, 9 and 12 onward repeat the request for forgiveness and mercy for parents, living and dead.
